Title: Departed workforce account remains enabled
Criteria: Departed workforce identities must be disabled at the approved termination time, active sessions revoked, and downstream application access checked.
Condition: USR-005 has an HR end date of 31 July 2026 but remains Enabled on the 24 August 2026 review date. The last simulated sign-in was 4 August 2026, after the employment end date.
Cause: The manual leaver process has no complete system checklist, timed trigger, independent validation, or exception escalation.
Risk: A former-user identity may access Microsoft 365 or connected applications, expose business data, or support fraud and unauthorized activity.
Recommendation: Disable the identity immediately, revoke sessions, review post-end-date activity, remove downstream access, transfer owned resources, and independently validate closure.
Validation_Step: Verify directory audit event shows account disabled status and zero post-closure authentication entries.

Title: MFA is not centrally enforced for standard workforce identities
Criteria: All human workforce identities require centrally enforced, non-bypassable Multi-Factor Authentication for all corporate system access.
Condition: Review of EV-IAM-003 indicates that central MFA enforcement is missing for 56 active standard workforce identities, including all 10 standard users sampled.
Cause: Conditional access rules have historically been restricted to high-privilege administrators to minimize daily friction for standard business users.
Risk: Threat actors can easily compromise standard user mailboxes and integrated SaaS applications via phishing or credential stuffing, using them for data theft or internal fraud.
Recommendation: Configure and enforce a global Conditional Access policy mandating MFA for all workforce logins and explicitly disable legacy protocols.
Validation_Step: Inspect the central directory authentication report to confirm a 100% active workforce coverage metric.

Title: Expired guest access remains enabled
Criteria: External contractor and guest access profiles must maintain a hardcoded expiration window and be deactivated automatically upon contract termination.
Condition: GST-002 and GST-004 remain active and enabled within the directory despite passing their documented access end dates of 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-15.
Cause: Guest accounts lack automated lifecycle policies or programmatic alerts to notify internal sponsors of expiration events.
Risk: External vendor profiles can accumulate access indefinitely, broadening the attack surface and increasing the business risk of supply chain pivot attacks.
Recommendation: Purge expired guest profiles immediately, execute automated session revocation commands, and implement access packages with strict expiration constraints.
Validation_Step: Confirm directory object query returns a hard-disabled or deleted status for both targeted accounts.

Title: Service identities permit interactive sign-in and one lacks ownership
Criteria: Non-human service accounts must be restricted to non-interactive token execution, mapped to a human owner, and blocked from portal web sign-ins.
Condition: SVC-001 and SVC-004 are misconfigured to allow interactive web browser sign-ins, and SVC-004 contains an empty Owner field in the registry.
Cause: Service accounts were provisioned using standard user creation templates rather than specialized workload identity security profiles.
Risk: Intercepted programmatic credentials can be utilized by threat actors to execute interactive web logins, bypassing code pipeline barriers to reach cloud infrastructure.
Recommendation: Assign an active internal human owner to SVC-004, and apply a Conditional Access policy explicitly blocking interactive sign-ins for all service accounts.
Validation_Step: Attempt an interactive portal login with service accounts and verify that the authentication attempt is rejected by policy.

Title: Mover retained former-role administration
Criteria: Mover access must match the new role, and former-role access must be removed within one business day of the effective change.
Condition: USR-007 moved from Support Lead to Finance Analyst on 1 August 2026 but retains Zendesk Administrator access. The target Finance Analyst role permits Stripe Read and no Zendesk administration.
Cause: Role changes grant new access additions without automatically comparing, reconciling, and purging prior-role system permissions.
Risk: Excessive customer-support administration access can expose sensitive customer tickets, permit unauthorized portal changes, and weaken separation of responsibility.
Recommendation: Remove Zendesk Administrator access, validate the remaining Finance permissions, and implement an old-role versus new-role difference check for every mover.
Validation_Step: Inspect Zendesk user administration dashboard to confirm the account permissions have been restricted strictly to the Finance baseline.

Title: Finance permissions create a separation-of-duties conflict
Criteria: Critical financial processing capabilities, such as creating transactions and final business approvals, must be separated across distinct human identities.
Condition: USR-008 holds both Stripe Refund Approver and corporate Finance Approval capabilities simultaneously within the application access dataset.
Cause: The finance department lacks documented segregation-of-duties (SoD) profiles within their software entitlement assignment process.
Risk: A single compromised or malicious identity can execute unauthorized financial distributions and self-approve the ledger items without dual-control oversight.
Recommendation: Submit the conflict to the CFO to strip one of the dual capabilities or implement a mandatory secondary approval control.
Validation_Step: Verify that Stripe and accounting software configurations actively prevent a single identity from holding both privileges.

Title: Standing privileged access has no quarterly review evidence
Criteria: Privileged access must be least-privileged, reviewed quarterly, and time-limited where supported.
Condition: Four active workforce identities have standing privileged roles, and no previous access-review date is recorded. Two identities hold Global Administrator access in the simulated dataset.
Cause: Privileged roles are assigned directly and have no recurring recertification or eligible-activation workflow.
Risk: Unnecessary or persistent privilege increases the effect of credential theft, misuse, error, and compromised daily-work accounts.
Recommendation: Review every privileged role, reduce broad administration, separate daily and admin identities, and plan eligible time-limited activation with strong MFA and approval where supported.
Validation_Step: Verify deployment of Privileged Identity Management (PIM) with eligible-only activation roles and archived quarterly review schedules.

Title: Stale enabled identities lack documented owner decisions
Criteria: Active identity accounts must be audited and disabled if they demonstrate zero interactive sign-in telemetry over a rolling 45-day operational threshold.
Condition: SVC-004, GST-002, GST-003, and USR-013 are currently enabled despite exceeding 45 days without a recorded interactive sign-in event.
Cause: The directory lacks automated stale account detection notifications or structured monthly inactive account validation routines.
Risk: Dangling inactive accounts provide a stealthy point of entry for attackers, allowing persistence on the corporate network without alerting regular users.
Recommendation: Execute an immediate review with system sponsors, disable accounts with no current business justification, and configure an automated stale account policy.
Validation_Step: Check tenant configuration records to confirm targeted stale profiles are set to a disabled state or possess an authorized exception.

Title: Joiner-mover-leaver governance is not formalized
Criteria: User lifecycle transitions must follow formalized, documented timelines with explicit completion criteria and signed manager verifications.
Condition: The current JML process operates on informal notes without structured timelines, mandatory checklists, or automated HR database synchronization tools.
Cause: The company's small IT team has historically managed onboarding and offboarding manually via direct ad-hoc messages and email notifications.
Risk: Absence of formalized lifecycle workflows causes widespread privilege drift, orphaned user directory objects, and unrevoked third-party access lanes.
Recommendation: Formally adopt the integrated JML workflow standard and build out automated Joiner-Mover-Leaver validation playlists inside the identity tier.
Validation_Step: Review signed JML process checklists for all recent workforce additions and role changes executed over the evaluation cycle.

Title: Emergency administrative access is not defined or tested
Criteria: Emergency break-glass accounts must be configured outside default MFA restrictions, securely vaulted, and monitored continuously for anomalous activation events.
Condition: The repository lacks documented emergency account procedures, exclusion testing records, or specialized break-glass monitoring alerts.
Cause: IT operations have focused on standard day-to-day administration without defining specific architecture recovery paths for conditional access lockout scenarios.
Risk: An internal policy misconfiguration or cloud-provider MFA disruption could permanently lock out all administrative identities, causing prolonged downtime.
Recommendation: Configure two cloud-isolated emergency access accounts, exclude them from standard Conditional Access rules, vault passwords physically, and write alert triggers.
Validation_Step: Inspect tenant monitoring dashboards to confirm active, high-priority notification rules trigger immediately upon any emergency account authentication.
